text:
incident-bot: ALERT service=redwood-serving env=prod metric=token_tail_latency_99 > 2.5s for 8m. Paging current oncall.

Derek: I'm on. Seeing sustained high queue depth and GPUs pegged (~98%) on gpulb-5 and gpulb-6.

Sara: Console shows bursty arrival of huge embedding jobs after 22:10Z. Average batch size jumped and continuous batching isn't able to absorb spikes. Some customers reporting intermittent 504s.

Chen: No config deploys in last 90m. Likely traffic pattern change from a partner bulk import.

Jordan: Which routes are hit hardest? Any paid customers affected?

Sara: /v1/embeddings is the biggest offender. /v1/generate sees increased tail for non-streaming fallbacks. A handful of free-tier and best-effort customers impacted; two paid customers seeing elevated retries but not breaching formal SLA escalation yet.

Maria: I'll prep a short customer notification once we have a mitigations plan.

Derek: Proposed mitigations (short-term): 1) Apply emergency rate limit to free-tier: 15rps; 2) Increase continuous batching window for embeddings to 100ms to improve GPU packing; 3) Temporarily disable streaming for embeddings and the heavy generate->rerank pipeline; 4) Canary config at 5% then 100% if stable; 5) Lower free-tier token budget to reduce max batch tokens.

Chen: Also enable automatic model fallbacks to quantized-small for best-effort customers to lower per-token GPU time.

ops-bot: Confirm you have approval to impose rate limits and send customer note.

Derek: Oncall lead approved. Maria will send the note.

Sara: Pushing batching config to staging. New config snippet for /v1/embeddings:```yaml
service: redwood-serving
route: /v1/embeddings
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  window_ms: 100
  max_batch_tokens: 65536
  backpressure_enabled: true
  prefix_cache: true
```
This raises window from 20ms to 100ms. Expected P95 increase ~+80-120ms for embeddings but should drastically cut GPU stalls.

Chen: For latency-sensitive generate route we'll set window_ms=30ms and max_batch_tokens=12288 to minimize customer impact.

Derek: Executing mitigation commands:```bash
# apply emergency rate limit for free-tier for 3h
redwoodctl traffic limit set --policy free-tier --rate 15/s --duration 3h --reason "emergency traffic shaping"
# apply batching config canary 5%
redwoodctl config apply --service redwood-serving --file batching-embeds-emergency.yaml --percent 5
```

ops-bot: Action recorded (incident-1954329999). Owner: derek.

Jordan: Watching canary. Abort if errors > 1% or p99 on paid routes increases by > 500ms.

Sara: Canary after 4 mins: target shards show queue depth down ~45%, GPU utilization to ~75%. Embeddings p95 rose from ~700ms to ~1.0s. Success rates improved, 500s reduced. No regression on paid generate routes.

maria: Drafting customer message: "We're observing elevated traffic impacting some embedding requests. We've applied temporary traffic shaping and batching changes that may increase latency for free and best-effort requests while restoring service availability. We'll update in 30 minutes." Send?

Derek: Send now and tag the two customers we know of.

maria: Sent. Customer-success confirmed outreach.

Chen: Rolling to 100% after 8m of stable canary. Applying fallback quantized model for best-effort customers as well.

Sara: Rolling command:```bash
redwoodctl config apply --service redwood-serving --file batching-embeds-emergency.yaml --percent 100
# enable model fallback for scope best-effort
redwoodctl model fallback set --scope best-effort --model redwood-quant-small --percent 100
```

Jordan: Monitoring: embeddings 500s down, GPU utilization stable ~69%, global p99 for embeddings ~1.2s (improved compared to alert).

Derek: Apply token budget cap for free-tier to limit largest requests:```bash
redwoodctl quota update --scope free-tier --param max_tokens 1024 --duration 24h
```

maria: Customers reported improvement. One partner was asked to chunk uploads and is coordinating to throttle their import job.

Chen: Filing post-incident follow-ups: a) traffic detection rules to auto-chunk large embedding requests, b) implement per-customer adaptive batching policies based on SLA and historical batch shapes.

Ops-bot: Reminder: annotate runbook with config diff and incident tags.

Derek: Config diff id: e4f1b2. I'll attach to the ticket.

Jordan: Handoff scheduled: night oncall chen will take over at 23:30Z. Leaving summary: emergency batching window increased to 100ms for embeddings, free-tier rate-limited to 15rps, streaming disabled for heavy routes, free-tier token cap 1024, quantized fallback enabled for best-effort. Monitor for 2 hours.

Chen: Taking over. Quick note: rollback command if we need to return to baseline:```bash
redwoodctl config apply --service redwood-serving --file batching-rollback.yaml --percent 100
redwoodctl traffic limit remove --policy free-tier
redwoodctl model fallback remove --scope best-effort
```

maria: Acknowledged. I'll update customers at 30 and 90 minutes. :thumbsup:

Derek: Closing initial mitigation. Will open RFC for adaptive batching and auto-chunking.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE (incident-1954329999) status=mitigated_by_config_changes assigned=chen

Chen: Adding a quick note before handoff: keep an eye on downstream rerank jobs; if rerank queue starts to backlog, consider re-enabling streaming for paid customers only or lowering their batching window further.

Maria: Noted. End of thread.
